title: AWS Solutions Architect Patterns
description: Explore common AWS solution patterns, anti-patterns, and real-world examples for choosing the right services.

data.text: AWS Solutions Architects rely on proven patterns to solve common problems. Understanding these patterns — and the anti-patterns to avoid — helps you design better systems faster.

data.title: Popular Patterns
items: **Static Website on S3 + CloudFront** — host a website without servers
**Serverless API** — API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB for REST APIs
**Real-Time Data Pipeline** — Kinesis → Lambda → S3 for streaming analytics
**Three-Tier Web App** — ALB + EC2/ECS + RDS for traditional apps
**Batch Processing** — Batch + S3 + Lambda for scheduled workloads
**CI/CD Pipeline** — CodePipeline + CodeBuild + CodeDeploy for automated releases

data.title: Common Mistakes
items: **Monolithic server** — running everything on one large EC2 instance instead of distributing
**Tight coupling** — services that depend on each other's internal implementation
**Single point of failure** — one database or one AZ for critical workloads
**Ignoring monitoring** — not setting up CloudWatch alarms and dashboards
**Over-engineering** — using microservices for a small application

data.text: A typical e-commerce platform on AWS uses CloudFront for the frontend, API Gateway + Lambda for the backend, DynamoDB for the product catalog, and SQS for order processing. Each service scales independently, and the system can handle traffic spikes during sales events.

data.title: Pattern Selection
data.text: Start simple. Use a 3-tier architecture for traditional apps and serverless for event-driven or variable workloads. Avoid microservices until you have a clear reason to split.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use proven patterns to solve common problems faster
Avoid anti-patterns like tight coupling and single points of failure
Start simple and evolve your architecture as your needs grow
